w: Swamishri asked a sadhu, "While we were coming to Sankari by road there was a village near Bhatiya. What is it called?"
"Lingad," the sadhu replied.

"Yes. We passed it. Some devotees were waiting for us, but we did not stop (because Swamishri was engrossed in reading). They must have felt bad. I will give you a letter (of apology) to give to them."
"Bapa, they will not have felt bad about it. They are true devotees," the sadhu replied.

Swamishri's concern for probably having hurt the feelings of ordinary, rural devotees is evident here. Though two days had passed since the incident had happened, Swamishri had not forgotten it during the busy volunteer training camp program. His love for the ordinary devotees is reflected here.
For Swamishri's satisfaction, the sadhu told him that he would bring the devotees for darshan.
The next day when the devotees met him, Swamishri expressed his regrets, "Forgive me. I was engrossed in reading and didn't realize immediately that you were waiting. So be happy."
The devotes replied, "Swami, we did not feel bad. In fact we were happy to have your darshan."
Swamishri then enquired everyone's name and blessed them.
We should worship God with the same responsibility as we do our worldly work.

At 5.55 p.m. Swamishri arrived in Gana from Bochasan. The devotees welcomed Swamishri with a marching band and torches fueled with ghee. After performing arti and pujan rituals of the deities in the newly established hari mandir Swamishri blessed the assembly.

At 7.20 p.m. Swamishri arrived at IRMA (Institute of Rural Management Anand) in Anand for the 5-day spiritual camp for 200 kishores and kishoris of UK and USA. Swamishri was welcomed by the kishores singing the Vedic Shanti-Path and honored with garlands by Chairman of IRMA Dr. Kurien, Director of IRMA Shri K. P. Reddy and Managing Director of G.C.M.M.F. Shri B. M. Vyas. The 5-day camp was themed 'Journey of Faith'. To enlighten and consolidate the kishores and kishoris about Indian culture and values the 5-day program was dedicated to Culture, Satsang, Samjan, Satpurush and Sanstha. Swamishri provided invaluable guidance and the sadhus and kishores presented lectures, recitations, kirtans and skits. Pujya Mahant Swami, Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami and Pujya Vivkesagar Swami also enlightened everyone with their discourses. ( See News report )
ph: Swamishri blesses the devotees after their presentation

w: Vishwashanti Mahayagna Hundreds of devotees gathered to pray for world peace and harmony by participating in the Vishwashanti Mahayagna, or World Peace Prayer.

Religious figures from different faiths, including Buddhism, Christianity, Islam, Jainism, Judaism, and Sikhism, attended the Mahayagna to symbolise unity among diverse religions. They all greeted Swamishri and offered a prayer for peace according to their respective faiths. The Lieutenant Governor of Ontario, Honourable James K. Bartleman, was also present on this occasion.

Swamishri concluded the prayers by blessing the assembly. He explained that in order to acquire peace, people must respect all religions, and must also see God in all by maintaining faith in their own religion. He thanked the religious figures and all who attended for being a part of the cause for peace.
Today marked an auspicious and historic landmark for the Swaminarayan Akshardham complex.

First, Swamishri performed the Vedic abhishek rituals for the golden kalashes of the Akshardham monument. Then, at 10.30 am he performed the Vedic rituals and arti for the placing of the 11 ft. Swamishri performed both these traditional rituals with meticulous care and great joy.
When Swamishri emerged from the main monument the main kalash had already been hoisted by crane and fixed on top of the central dome.
Praying on behalf of all the youths, Pratik Shah said,
"We have jobs, we do satsang work, and we also carry the responsibilities of home. Often it is very hard to set priorities. Please bless us so that we can do every task well."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said at once, "Just as a school sets a timetable, keep a firm resolve and set up a timetable, and everything will fall into place. Wake up at this time, bathe, and so on. If you keep that resolve, it all gets completed. If you do not set a timetable, you lie in bed out of laziness and the work does not get done."
Swamishri inspired them.
